name: Fort McAllister State Park
unique: The best preserved earthwork fort on the Georgia coast, with the original bombproof shelters and a massive earthen wall that held out ironclads for years, sitting on a salt marsh at the mouth of the Ogeechee.
buzz: The earthworks are intact enough to walk through and the marsh boardwalk is full of birds. Camping under the oaks is the local secret.

name: J.F. Gregory Park
unique: A park on the site of Henry Ford's old sawmill and lumber village, with a boardwalk through cypress wetlands, a pond and a trail system that locals use every morning.
buzz: The boardwalk and the cypress are the draw, and the park connects to the heritage trail markers about Ford's winter town. Free and flat.

name: Coastal Bryan Heritage Trail
unique: A driving and walking route through rice plantations, Liberty ships, a Civil War fort and the remains of Henry Ford's experimental southern town, with markers at each stop.
buzz: Ford built a whole village here in the 1920s and almost nobody outside the county knows. The trail signposts it well enough to do on your own.

name: Fort Stewart Museum
unique: The museum of the 3rd Infantry Division, with vehicles, uniforms and the division's history from the Marne through two Iraq invasions, on the largest army post east of the Mississippi.
buzz: Visitors need a pass to get on post, and the collection is worth the paperwork. The armored vehicles outside are the photographs.

name: Dorchester Academy
unique: A school for freedpeople that became the planning site for the Birmingham campaign, where Martin Luther King Jr and the movement's leaders met in 1963 in a room still standing.
buzz: The dormitory room where they met is preserved and the guides tell it from memory. A national landmark that gets almost no traffic.

name: Midway Church and Museum
unique: A 1754 meeting house rebuilt in 1792, with a slave gallery, a cemetery holding two signers of the Declaration and the graves of Continental officers, in a settlement older than the county.
buzz: The cemetery is the reason historians stop, with Revolutionary names and a row of Confederate dead. The building is plain and enormous.

name: Fort King George State Historic Site
unique: The reconstructed palisade and blockhouse of the southernmost British fort in North America, built in 1721 to hold the Altamaha, on a bluff over the river marsh.
buzz: The rebuild is convincing and the story of the garrison dying of disease is told straight. Alligators in the moat ditch are a real feature.

name: Harris Neck National Wildlife Refuge
dates: Year round, daylight, some areas closed in season
unique: A former army airfield and before that a Black owned settlement, now a refuge of salt marsh and old oaks where wood storks nest in numbers and the taxiways make a flat bike loop.
buzz: The wood stork rookery in spring is the spectacle, hundreds of birds in the trees over the water. The old runway is a strange and good place to ride.

name: Sapelo Island
dates: Tours Tuesday to Saturday, reservations required
unique: A barrier island reachable only by state ferry, with the Gullah Geechee community of Hog Hammock still living on it, a mansion ruin in the dunes and a lighthouse at the north end.
buzz: The island is not a resort and the tours are the only way in. People come back talking about Hog Hammock and the Reynolds mansion ruin, not the beach.

name: Darien Waterfront and Altamaha Delta
customer: Boaters, history walkers, shrimpers at heart
unique: A shrimp boat waterfront on a bluff above the Altamaha delta, with a 1736 grid of tabby ruins, a small museum and boat trips out to the barrier islands.
buzz: The waterfront shrimp market is the reason to come in season, and the delta boat tours get you to sandbars nobody else reaches.

name: Jesup Train Day and ArchFest
unique: A downtown festival built around the railroad that made Jesup, with model trains, a story walk and the ArchFest art and music on the same blocks.
buzz: The model railroad layouts draw the kids and the depot platform draws the rail fans. Small, free and genuinely local.

name: Jesup Atlantic Coast Line Depot
dates: Daily, train viewing from the platform
unique: A 1903 Atlantic Coast Line depot with a brick platform and a waiting room still in use, where Amtrak's Silver Service stops and freight comes through all day.
buzz: The station was restored and won a preservation award. Bring a scanner and a folding chair and the afternoon goes quickly.

name: Poppell Farms
dates: Autumn for the maze, spring for strawberries
customer: Families with young kids, school groups
unique: A Wayne County farm that opens its fields for u-pick strawberries in spring and a corn maze, hayride and pumpkin patch in autumn, with a country store at the front.
buzz: The maze and the hayride are the October draw and the strawberries are picked clean by noon in April. Bring boots.

name: Jesup Drive-In
unique: One of the last drive-in theatres running in Georgia, with a double feature on weekends, a gravel lot and a screen you watch from the truck bed.
buzz: People drive from Savannah and Jacksonville for it. The snack bar is cash and the sound comes over the radio.

name: Appling County Heritage Center
unique: A county heritage museum with the timber, turpentine and tobacco history of the Altamaha country, plus the records of the families who cleared it.
buzz: Volunteers run it and know every name in the files. Good starting point before driving out to Moody Forest.

name: Moody Forest Natural Area
dates: Guided walks by arrangement, spring and autumn
unique: Four thousand acres of old growth longleaf pine and blackwater swamp along the Altamaha, one of the largest remaining old growth longleaf stands left anywhere, with trees older than the county.
buzz: Access is limited and arranged through the conservancy, which keeps it intact. Red cockaded woodpeckers and the open pine cathedral are what people describe.

name: A. Randall Tuten Environmental Park
unique: A city park with a pond, a boardwalk and a walking trail through pine and cypress, built on the edge of town where the flatwoods begin.
buzz: An easy loop with herons and turtles, and it costs nothing. The locals walk it before work.

name: Jack Hill State Park
unique: A state park with a lake, a beach and an eighteen hole course, home to the Gordonia tree that was thought extinct until a stand was found nearby, and renamed for a state senator in 2021.
buzz: The golf course is the reason many people come and it is cheap for what it is. The lake and picnic areas are quiet midweek.

name: The Olive Grove
dates: Tours by reservation, harvest in autumn
unique: An olive grove and mill in south Georgia, growing and pressing oil in a climate nobody associates with olives, with a tour that walks the trees and the press.
buzz: The novelty is real and the oil is good. Tours are booked ahead and the harvest season is the time to go.

name: Georgia Veterans Memorial Cemetery
unique: A state veterans cemetery laid out in formal rows with a carillon and a memorial walk, in a county that sends its young people to the military generation after generation.
buzz: People come for a specific name and stay for the walk. Quiet, and the flag avenue is the photograph.

name: The Claxton Bakery
customer: Fruitcake believers, families, food history people
unique: The bakery that made Claxton the fruitcake capital, selling millions of pounds a year from a storefront on Main Street, where you can watch the mixing and buy a warm slice.
buzz: People who hate fruitcake change their mind here. Christmas season is a production line running at full speed.

name: Claxton Rattlesnake and Wildlife Festival
unique: Nearly fifty years of a festival built on the eastern diamondback, with captive snakes, a milking demonstration, wildlife exhibits and a parade, run with the state DNR on handling and conservation.
buzz: The snake handling demonstration is the draw and it is genuinely educational, not a stunt show. Busy on Saturday.

name: Hames Hall
unique: A large early twentieth century country house on the highway north of Claxton, listed on the National Register, standing in fields the way planter houses here always did.
buzz: Visible from the road and worth a slow pass for anyone who likes southern domestic architecture. Not open to the public.

name: Morgan Lake Wildlife Management Area
unique: A coastal plain management area of pine flatwoods and cypress lakes with a boat ramp, good bream and bass fishing, and enough water to paddle all morning without seeing anyone.
buzz: Locals fish it hard in spring. Alligators are present and the boat ramp is basic.

name: Ludowici Well Pavilion
unique: A small pavilion over the mineral well that gave the town its health resort era, when northerners came south to drink the water and the Ludowici tile company built a town around it.
buzz: The town takes its name from a roofing tile company, which is its own story. The pavilion is a five minute stop with a good plaque.

name: Time Travelers Renaissance Faire
unique: A renaissance faire in a Long County field with jousting, armored combat, craft vendors and a crowd that comes in full kit, ten miles from the nearest interstate exit.
buzz: Small enough that the performers talk to you, and the armored combat is real steel. Check the date, it moves.

name: Georgia Salzburger Living History Site
unique: The site of Ebenezer, where Lutheran refugees from Salzburg landed in 1734 and built a town, with the 1769 Jerusalem church, a cemetery of original settlers and a living history museum.
buzz: The church and the cemetery are original and the story of the Salzburgers is one most southern history trips miss. Quiet and free.

name: Mars Theatre
unique: A 1945 movie house restored as a community arts venue, showing films and hosting touring music and theatre on a main street that has kept its storefronts.
buzz: Cheap tickets and a room with a real balcony. It has become the social centre of the county.

name: Butterducks Winery
unique: A muscadine and fruit wine vineyard on the coastal plain with a tasting room, a porch and vines that survive the heat where European grapes will not.
buzz: Sweet muscadine wines, a porch and live music on weekends. Not a Napa experience and does not pretend to be.

name: Studier's Honeypot
unique: A working honey operation selling Tupelo, gallberry and wildflower honey from hives in the coastal plain swamps, with the extracting equipment on site.
buzz: The Tupelo is the one to buy and it sells out. Ask about the bloom calendar, the beekeeper will explain the whole year.
